blocks.x: Back in 2007, no one imagined that Basic Sanitation, The Movie could feature two future Golden Globe winners (let alone three). It's widely known how difficult it is for any actor to achieve international stardom and run for awards, so that just isn't something filmmakers usually consider when developing a project. The premise is as quirky as it is absurd, following the efforts of a tiny village in southern Brazil to pipeline a local brook that carries all the town's waste. The townspeople learn that there is no allocated budget for infrastructure projects in the government, but there is, however, funding for a short film as part of an effort to foster artistic projects. blocks.x: As fun as it is to imagine a Golden Globe "hat-trick," Brazilian cinephiles are also somewhat skeptical about the odds of Gugu's World actually scoring a nomination. It wasn’t featured in the Cannes or Venice festivals, for example, so it has a much steeper climb compared to I'm Still Here and The Secret Agent, which also had influential names like Walter Salles and Kleber Mendonça Filho as directors. Because of that, there's significantly less coverage and expectations around Gugu's World.

None of that means that the Brazilian Film Academy made the wrong choice, of course. Quite the contrary, as, this time, there wasn't a clear outlier that it would be crazy not to pick. Gugu's World is definitely worthy, then. It was featured in this year's Berlinale and provides a very sensitive portrayal of growing up queer in more distant regions of Brazil. That's exactly where Lázaro Ramos comes in, playing the title character's estranged father, a truck driver who struggles to understand and come to terms with his son's queer identity.

So, even if the "prophecy" of Basic Sanitation doesn’t come true, Gugu's World being selected and Lázaro Ramos' work are still testament to Brazil's success as a film-making country. Of course, it would be incredible to have three consecutive Oscar nominees and Golden Globe winners, but, unfortunately, that's just not how the awards season game works. But we can dream. Who knows? Maybe it all works out and Lázaro brings home our country's third Golden Globe. Even if it doesn't happen, though, we are still immensely proud.
Basic Sanitation, The Movie is available to watch on YouTube and Prime Video.

‘Basic Sanitation, The Movie’ Has Foreseen Brazil’s Golden Globe Winners for the Past Two Years

Image via Vitrine Filmes

Image via Vitrine Filmes

There also wasn't much buzz when it came out, but, thanks to its now internationally-recognized star-studded cast, it's going through a renaissance of sorts. Filmmaker Jorge Furtado was also a household name by then (everyone remembers watching his short feature Isle of Flowers at school, for example), so all the hype really is overdue.

The new film comes from the director of Tom Hardy's 'The Revenant.'
